features.definition: 1 if the Pokémon has a bird-like body (beak, feathers, wings as primary limbs), 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon has an aquatic body form (fish, dolphin, whale, seahorse, octopus, etc.), 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon resembles an insect, arachnid, or arthropod, 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon resembles a four-legged mammal (dog, cat, bear, etc.), 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon has a clearly humanoid/bipedal body with two arms and two legs, 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon visibly has a shell (turtle shell, snail shell, ammonite shell), 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon has visible wings (feathered, membranous, or insect wings), 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon has tentacles, fins, or similar appendages, 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon incorporates plant elements (leaves, flowers, vines, bark), 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon is primarily made of rock, stone, mineral, or metallic material, 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon visually suggests ice (icy blue-white coloring, ice crystals, frozen features), 0 otherwise
Degree to which green is the dominant color: 0 = no green, 1 = entirely green
Degree to which blue is the dominant color: 0 = no blue, 1 = entirely blue
Degree to which brown/tan/beige is the dominant color: 0 = none, 1 = entirely brown/tan
Degree to which dark colors (black, dark grey, dark purple) dominate: 0 = none, 1 = entirely dark
Perceived body bulk/size: 0 = very small and compact, 1 = very large and massive
1 if the Pokémon has very large or prominently featured eyes relative to body, 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon has a ghostly, cosmic, or ethereal appearance (floating, translucent, cloud-like, starry), 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon has visible claws, pincers, or scythes as notable features, 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon has a clearly visible tail, 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon has visible spikes, horns, or sharp protrusions on its body, 0 otherwise
Degree of roundness/cuteness: 0 = angular/menacing, 1 = very round and cute
1 if the Pokémon stands upright on two legs, 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon is visibly covered in fur or feathers, 0 otherwise
1 if the Pokémon has a hard outer shell or exoskeleton (not counting turtle shells), 0 otherwise
Degree to which orange or red-orange is the dominant color: 0 = no orange/red-orange, 1 = entirely orange/red-orange
Degree to which grey (medium grey, stone grey, not dark black or light white) dominates the color palette: 0 = no grey, 1 = entirely grey
1 if the Pokémon has an overall menacing, aggressive, or threatening appearance (fierce expression, combat stance, dangerous features); 0 if neutral or cute

notes: item_299 (Geodude, grey-brown rock) should cluster with brown/tan/earthy, small-medium, natural Pokémon. It should be far from blue, dark, large, aggressive ones. The dominant grouping criterion appears to be primary color palette (brown/tan/earthy vs blue/green/dark) combined with size and aggression. Need to heavily boost brown_tan color weight, reduce blue color influence, and possibly add an earthy/natural color feature.
